content: 1. Exercise caution when co-administering peramivir with nephrotoxic drugs, as this combination may increase the risk of renal toxicity. Monitor renal function closely. 2. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or efficacy of oral neomycin by enhancing its efflux through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) transporter. Use caution and monitor therapeutic response. 3. Phenytoin decreases the levels or effects of oral neomycin via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 4. Quercetin reduces the levels or effects of oral neomycin by modulating the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of oral neomycin through the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 6. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of oral neomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 7. Sirolimus enhances the levels or effects of oral neomycin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Exercise caution and monitor closely. 8. Oral neomycin reduces the efficacy of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering its metabolism. Monitor for reduced therapeutic effects. 9. Co-administration of antibiotics with sodium picosulfate decreases its efficacy by disrupting colonic bacterial flora required for drug activation. Monitor for suboptimal response. 10. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases the toxicity of oral neomycin through mechanisms related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. 11. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases the toxicity of oral neomycin, likely due to fluid and electrolyte disturbances. Monitor closely for adverse events. 12. Oral neomycin reduces the levels of sorafenib through an unknown mechanism, with a 54% decrease in AUC observed in healthy volunteers. Use caution and monitor therapeutic response. 13. St. John’s Wort decreases the levels or effects of oral neomycin by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Co-administration of oral neomycin and streptomycin increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 15.
